nnSVG parameters

Source: R/tool-nnsvg.R
nnsvgParam.Rd

Parameters for GiottoClass::analyzeData() that run nnSVG (Weber et al. 2023), which finds spatially variable genes by fitting a nearest-neighbor Gaussian process to each gene and testing it against a model without spatial terms (likelihood ratio test). nnSVG is a Bioconductor package, install it with BiocManager::install("nnSVG"). If you use it, please cite the original paper (see References).

Usage

nnsvgParam(
  n_neighbors = 10L,
  order = c("AMMD", "Sum_coords"),
  n_threads = 1L,
  seed = 1L
)

# S4 method for class 'allMatrix,nnsvgParam'
analyzeData(x, param, spatial_locs, X = NULL, ...)

Arguments

n_neighbors

integer, nearest neighbors of the Gaussian process (nnSVG's default 10; 5 is faster with similar results)

order

ordering of the spots for the nearest-neighbor approximation: "AMMD" (nnSVG's default) or "Sum_coords" (for fewer than 65 spots)

n_threads

integer, genes fitted in parallel

seed

integer seed set before nnSVG runs (its fits draw random numbers, so results vary slightly between runs without one); NULL leaves the random number generator alone. The caller's random state is restored afterwards

x

normalized (log) expression matrix, features x cells

param

a nnsvgParam

spatial_locs

two-column matrix of coordinates, rows in the column order of x

X

NULL or a covariate model matrix (cells x covariates, with an intercept column), e.g. model.matrix(~ cell_type)

Value

A nnsvgParam object.

Details

analyzeData(x, param, spatial_locs, X) returns a data.table with one row per feature (feat_ID) and nnSVG's columns: the fitted sigma.sq (spatial variance), tau.sq (nonspatial variance), phi (length scale), loglik, runtime, mean, var, spcov (spatial coefficient of variation), prop_sv (proportion of spatial variance), loglik_lm, LR_stat, rank (by LR_stat), pval and padj (BH). mean, var and spcov are computed from x, as nnSVG does for the logcounts of a SpatialExperiment.

References

Weber LM, Saha A, Datta A, Hansen KD, Hicks SC. nnSVG for the scalable identification of spatially variable genes using nearest-neighbor Gaussian processes. Nature Communications 14, 4059 (2023). doi:10.1038/s41467-023-39748-z

See also

runNnSVG()

Examples

p <- nnsvgParam(n_neighbors = 5)
p$n_neighbors
